page: Microsoft Azure E8s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. Backed by 64 GB of system RAM, it maintains an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. The x86_64 architecture is outfitted with a substantial 480 MB L3 cache and supports specialized instruction extensions including Intel AMX, AVX-512, and advanced cryptographic acceleration.

Hardware configurations exclude integrated local ephemeral storage and GPU coprocessors, requiring network-attached storage options like Azure Premium Storage for disk operations. In benchmark evaluations, the instance performs consistently within average thresholds for general multi-core compute, achieving 8,040.17 on stress-ng and 14,704.33 on PassMark CPU tests. It demonstrates strong single-threaded data compression capabilities, recording 33.58 GB/sec in gzip benchmarks and 13.92 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, while sustaining 14.37 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations.

Operationally, the instance presents an efficient resource envelope for memory-intensive duties without the added overhead of unutilized accelerator hardware. While larger deep learning inferences like 70B parameter models show performance bottlenecks, the memory density and CPU throughput align effectively with in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, relational database management systems, and analytical data pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E8s_v7 is a memory-optimized cloud instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 64 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates a 480 MB L3 cache along with AVX-512 and AMX instructions for accelerated integer and matrix computations. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote persistent storage solutions. Benchmark profiles demonstrate mid-tier multi-core compute capability alongside strong single-threaded data compression throughput, reaching 33.58 GB/sec on gzip tasks and 14.37 million Redis SET operations per second. With an 8 GB per vCPU density profile, the E8s_v7 represents a balanced hardware allocation for caching layers, in-memory databases, memory-bound analytical processing, and medium-scale enterprise application workloads.
